set.body:
Need (storyatlas4s Recall Voyage, 2026-09-03): intaglio paints literal `Rgba` as presentation
attributes (`fill`, `stroke`, `fill-opacity`), never `style=`, so a host CSS rule can override them
— but only by `[data-name]` or by element type, because a grob carries no class and no attribute
beyond its one name (GraphicsTypes.scala:3-12). The voyage page has a token-driven light/dark
stylesheet; the intaglio plate cannot follow the theme, and storyatlas4s cannot address "all
decode-filled marks" or "all coding bands" from CSS without inventing names that are not MarkIds
(its contract: one `data-name` per mark, equal to the MarkId, never anything else).

Proposal: an optional `cssClass: Option[String]` (space-separated tokens, validated) and an
optional small `data: Map[String, String]` (keys validated as `data-*` names) on `Grob`, emitted by
the SVG backend as `class` and `data-<key>` attributes; ignored by raster backends. Optionally a
paint mode that emits `var(--token, #rrggbb)` for a named `Rgba` so a page's tokens win when
present and the literal colour stands alone otherwise.

Acceptance:
- class and data attributes appear on the emitted element/group; absent ones change nothing;
- laws: attribute-name validation refuses names that are not `data-*`-safe or class tokens with
  whitespace; determinism; geometry unchanged by styling (a conformance law);
- storyatlas4s can express origin-as-shape and kind-as-class together, and the reference page's
  dark theme applies to the plate through its tokens.
set.title: [Intaglio 1.x][SVG][Theming] Class names and data attributes on grobs, so a host stylesheet can theme
